مَهْبُوتٌ Confounded; perplexed; amazed; i. q. مَهْفُوتٌ. (TA, art. هفت.) مَهْبُوتُ الفُؤَادِ A man of a cowardly heart, without intellect. (S.) See هَبِيتٌ ―
-b2- مَهْبُوتٌ Lowered with respect to rank, station, or dignity. (Fr.) ―
-b3- مَهْبُوتُ التَّرَاقِى Having depressed, deficient, collar-bones, or clavicles. (Fr.) ＝
-A2- مَهْبُوتٌ A bird that is sent forth at random; without being rightly directed; [without being let fly at some other particular bird]. Thought by IDrd to be a post-classical word in this sense. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
